items.pregunta: Does the webhook or callback handler verify the sender's signature over the raw body (HMAC with a constant-time comparison, or a public key) before acting, and refuse the request when the signature or the secret is missing?
items.evidencia: The signature computation and comparison, and the branch taken when the header or the secret is absent

items.pregunta: Does the consumer take the tenant, user or account from the authenticated producer or the signed envelope, rather than from fields of the message body that the sender chooses?
items.evidencia: Where the handler reads the tenant or account it acts on

items.pregunta: Is every message decoded with a data-only parser (JSON, protobuf) and checked against the expected event types, never with a deserialiser that can build arbitrary classes or evaluate code?
items.evidencia: The decode call and the switch or schema over the event type

items.pregunta: Is a replayed or redelivered message (same event id, or a timestamp outside the tolerance) refused or made harmless before its side effect?
items.evidencia: The event id or timestamp check and where it runs relative to the side effect

items.pregunta: Does the consumer refuse an event older than the state it already holds (version, sequence or status check), so a late message cannot overwrite a newer state?
items.evidencia: The version or status comparison before the update

items.pregunta: Do dead-letter queues, retry logs and error topics keep secrets and full payloads of other tenants out of readers that should not see them?
items.evidencia: What the failure path logs or forwards and who reads that destination
